svg.title: ruPro workspace · learning across runs
svg.desc: Claude proposes a retry rule, Codex tests it, and the owner approves lesson M17. Catalog recalls M17 on a new read timeout. A simulated Catalog replay compares six passing cases without memory to eight with the lesson. Billing then checks a timed out payment against its receipt and records the owner’s decision. An architecture decision record preserves the reason for the rule. A later replay reveals a missed deadline and the owner approves a successor.

g.font-family: Avenir Next, Century Gothic, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Why did the second read succeed?
The first GET timed out. A retry worked.
Try one retry on reads only.
Test Claude’s rule before we reuse it.
Checking reads, writes and repeat timeouts.
I’ll attach the results for review.
Lesson M17 saved with its test evidence.
A catalog read timed out. Any prior lesson?
Found M17 in Checkout’s approved lessons.
It applies to a timed out GET.
The retry returned 200. Writes stay untouched.
Now replay all eight cases with and without M17.
Both runs replay the same eight fresh cases.
A payment timed out. Can we retry?
M17 covers reads. This was a POST.
The payment may already have settled.
Check the receipt before doing anything.
I’ll read the ledger by payment ID.
Payment ID matched one ledger entry.
Receipt and decision saved with run 3.
Why: repeating a charge can bill twice.
ADR A1 accepted. Lesson M17 cites A1.
A read timed out. What did Checkout learn?
Memory found M17, backed by ADR A1.
One retry is allowed for this GET.
Did the retry help before the deadline?
The retry succeeded after the caller left.
Record the late result as a failed case.
Replay: the old rule missed the caller deadline.
A1: retry a timed out GET
A2 supersedes A1. M17 now cites A2.
